title: Unified title
summary: UniJEPA introduces a joint framework for both photometric and temporal prediction in latent space for world modeling, while G$^2$WAM and Affordance-Aware World-Action Modeling provide efficient, geometry-grounded image-goal navigation and trajectory planning. Dual-Latent World Model (Dual-WM) and Controllable Crowd Generation with World-Model Planning address the challenges of executing actions in complex environments.

facts.statement: UniJEPA jointly learns photometric and temporal prediction in a shared latent space for efficient world modeling.
G$^2$WAM encodes spatial cues through a learned scene-coordinate localization module for efficient navigation.
Affordance-Aware World-Action Modeling improves trajectory planning by learning future action-relevant regions and spatial structure.
Ctrl-CWM integrates crowd generation and run-time control to simulate human behavior in real-world scenarios.
VPFlow replaces temporal-difference bootstrapping with a closed-form Monte Carlo return for offline goal reaching.

sources.title: Exploring Temporal Context-Aware Physical Grounding in Latent World Models
sources.description:
arXiv:2610.28483v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Learning latent dynamics is fundamental to building action-conditioned world models for planning. Among existing families, Joint Embedding Predictive Architectures (JEPAs) offer a natural framework by modeling transitions directly in latent space rather than at the pixel level. However, two issues remain in JEPA-based world models: (i) physical grounding lacks explicit aggregation of temporal context and (ii) action planning always overly relies on generic sampling distributions. To this end, we propose $\mathcal{G}$-JEPA, which incorporates temporal context into physical grounding for latent world models and couples the learned models with prior-guided action planning. Specifically, during learning, we incorporate a shared causal temporal module that aggregates temporal context within observation and prediction sequences under physical state supervision, grounding both in task-relevant physical states. When planning, we further introduce action inference through stepwise conditioning of a generative action distribution on the current and goal latent representations together with their evolving discrepancy, yielding anchored proposals that guide model-based online refinement. Together, physical state supervision guides temporal representation learning, while the action prior guides search through the learned world model. Experiments demonstrate improved planning performance on manipulation tasks, including tasks with increasing temporal separation between initial and goal observations. Code is publicly available at https://github.com/myl11045/G-JEPA.

sources.title: VPFlow: Value-Predictive Planning with Imperfect World Models for Offline Goal Reaching
sources.description:
arXiv:2610.27280v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: Offline goal-conditioned reinforcement learning enables skill acquisition by reaching any goal from any state without dense rewards. Model-based methods allow for planning by scaling test-time compute to solve complex tasks. Combining both holds appealing promise for pre-training on suboptimal demonstrations and zero-shot adaptation via goal specification and planning. Yet existing methods assume effective planning requires accurate next-state prediction in pixel or latent space. In this work, we show that value prediction is more useful for planning, whereas accurate state prediction is often unnecessary. Our key insight is that offline goal reaching naturally admits a closed-form Monte Carlo return, enabling value regression to replace temporal-difference bootstrapping. We use this return as the sole supervision for latent world models: imagined latents are trained to predict goal-reaching value rather than match future states, implicitly preventing representation collapse. These planning-oriented representations let imperfect world models imagine on the level sets of value field beyond dataset transitions. We then present VPFlow, a value-predictive planner that pairs the world models with a one-step flow policy and plans in its noise space via evolutionary search. It enables policy improvement with imagined generalized advantage and reduces out-of-distribution queries common in action-space planning. On 30 state and pixel OGBench datasets, VPFlow surpasses model-free baselines by at least 30.3 and 10.1 percentage points in success rate, respectively, and outperforms latent planners LeWorldModel, PLDM, and TD-MPC2. It achieves this despite a latent prediction error orders of magnitude larger than with state prediction, while minimizing this error lowers success rate. This demonstrates that value-predictive representations, not exact state prediction, are what offline planning requires.
